text:
Travis Konecny spent last week reading his own name in trade reports, then played his best game of the season. After a report that the Flyers had opened the door to moving him (Montreal Hockey Fanatics and NHLTradeRumor.com both ran with it), he had four points in Ottawa on Thursday, including the overtime winner, Philadelphia's first OT win of the season. PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor wrote that Konecny brought a dead-looking team back to life.

The season overall has been quieter: 11 points in 16 games, three goals on 4 expected, shooting 9.4%. The Flyers have scored 3.4 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on, and his scoring rate sits below our range for him (2.2 to 3.0 points per 60). His team is 6.3 points of expected-goal share better with him than without.

Evolving-Hockey's read on last season was the worry: barely above replacement, with opponents getting more chances when he was out there, bottom 6% of forwards. He also throws a lot of hits for a scorer, 49 already. Watch whether Thursday was a turn or a one-off, because it changes what Philadelphia decides.
